additions.title: A one-quadrant homoclinic disk contains a center
additions.statement: Let X be the characteristic C¹ field of a C² characteristic disk with finitely many nondegenerate centers and saddles. Let K be the bounded source disk of a simple directed homoclinic circuit through a saddle q. Suppose K occupies precisely one of the four local saddle sectors at q. If c_K and s_K count the centers and saddles strictly inside K, then c_K−s_K=1. In particular K contains a center. The saddle q is not included in s_K.
additions.strategy: Cut the circuit at two regular sections in a sufficiently small saddle box. In that box the local transverse first integral u has a nondegenerate saddle and the one-sector component of u−u(q) of the appropriate sign is bounded by the two chosen separatrix branches. Replace the corner by a small regular level arc in that sector. The implicit-function theorem gives a C² arc up to both section collars. Push the remaining compact regular circuit slightly into K, matching the two collars; in finitely many regular first-integral charts the pushed arc can be chosen so that X has positive component along its directed tangent. Near the joining collars this is preserved by sufficiently small C¹ interpolation. The resulting closed curve C lies in K, bounds all its interior zeros, excludes q, and its directed unit tangent has positive inner product with either X/|X| everywhere or its negative everywhere. Thus the straight homotopy between the normalized field and that directed tangent is nonzero. The tangent of this rounded simple curve has degree 1 with the positive boundary orientation (reversing both tangent directions changes the angle by the constant π and not its degree). This can be proved by the finite polygonal turning argument after polygonizing its regular arcs in disjoint tubular collars. The same punctured-polygon argument as the characteristic index-count supplier now gives c_K−s_K=deg(X|C)=1. No assertion about the three-sector outer loop or the two-sector pinched region follows from this calculation.

additions.title: A simple center frontier has a C² rounded endpoint trace
additions.statement: Suppose a center period annulus has outer frontier one simple homoclinic circuit Γ through one saddle, with no other singularities on Γ. There is ε>0 and a jointly C² leaf-valued transverse trace H:S¹×[0,ε]→M such that H_0 is leafwise homotopic to h|Γ and, for every t>0, H_t is leafwise freely homotopic to the image of the corresponding prescribed nearby closed characteristic orbit on the center-annulus side. No pointwise C² convergence of the original saddle-passing parametrizations is asserted. Consequently an essential endpoint gives a vanishing cycle if the nearby characteristic loops are leafwise null.
additions.strategy: Choose a small saddle source disk mapped into one foliation box (Y,z), and two regular cross-sections through the circuit branches away from the saddle. Parameterize each section by the transverse first integral t=z∘h−z(h(q)), reversing sign if necessary. Their endpoints on each nearby level are C² in t by the C² implicit-function theorem. Outside the saddle disk, finitely many regular first-integral charts transport one endpoint to the other; their maps and the compact edge trace are jointly C² down to t=0. The nearby closed orbits show that this edge transport and the local saddle passage have identical transverse coordinates for all sufficiently small t>0. The resulting return germ is therefore identity on that one-sided interval and at 0. This is an identity on an interval, not a conclusion from a limiting sequence of arbitrary return maps. In the saddle target plaque, replace the corner path at t=0 by a C² arc with the same endpoint collars. Extend this arc to small t by varying its Y coordinates C² and prescribing the plaque coordinate z=z(h(q))+t. To match the full endpoint collars, use finite intervals with a partition of unity in Y, leaving the prescribed collars untouched; all interpolations take place in a smaller convex plaque coordinate disk. The nearby original saddle paths and replacements lie in the same contractible plaque, so are homotopic relative to their collars. Glue this replacement to the C² regular edge trace on overlapping open collars. The return identity closes the loop for each t. In each box the transverse coordinate along a point track is a C² local diffeomorphism of t, so its derivative is nonzero, including at 0. The open-collar gluing supplier gives a jointly C² trace. This proves the stated homotopy relation, which is exactly what nullity and the vanishing-cycle definition use. It does not prove the stronger assertion that the unmodified hyperbolic level parametrizations themselves extend C² to the endpoint.

additions.title: A nested pinched center frontier gives a strict inner-disk search
additions.statement: Suppose the frontier of a center basin is two simple homoclinic loops through the same saddle q, with one loop nested inside the other. Their inner bounded disk K occupies one saddle quadrant, contains a center, and does not contain the selected basin center. Searching from any center of K remains inside K. If another nested two-loop frontier occurs in that search, its inner disk K′ is properly contained in K and has strictly fewer interior saddles. This is a selection statement in the original source disk; it does not assign an essential boundary class to K.
additions.strategy: The four half-branches at q alternate incoming and outgoing. A simple directed loop joins an adjacent incoming/outgoing pair. In the nested embedding the inner loop has its bounded side in one quadrant and the outer loop has its bounded side in three; their difference, the pinched basin, occupies the two remaining sectors. The one-quadrant index lemma gives a center inside K. The selected basin and K are disjoint, so that center differs from the selected center. The boundary of K is invariant. Uniqueness for the C¹ characteristic field prevents regular trajectories from crossing it; hence all nested periodic disks from a center in K remain there. Their frontier may reach its boundary circuit, but if it does then it is that one simple circuit, not a new nested pair. Any new nested pair therefore has a saddle r strictly inside K. Its inner disk K′ is contained in K and excludes r, while r was counted among the interior saddles of K. Thus s(K′)≤s(K)−1. The boundaries are source circuits; their image classes need not be essential and are not silently used as such.

additions.title: Center-frontier selection and cancellation have a finite rank
additions.statement: Assume the period-frontier supplier and the conditional simple-lobe cancellation supplier apply to the current characteristic disk, and singular images lie in distinct leaves. Starting at a center, the search terminates at an essential regular/simple-loop endpoint, the prescribed essential leafwise boundary, or a simple one-center/one-saddle lobe whose rounded endpoint is null. In the last case one fixed leafwise cap and the cancellation supplier remove exactly one center and one saddle relative to the outer collar. Iterating this operation terminates; no annulus-face no-revisit assumption is needed.
additions.strategy: Take the maximal annulus at once. The period-frontier supplier gives a regular orbit or a finite connected saddle graph. Distinct singular leaves prohibit edges between different saddle vertices; connectedness reduces a saddle frontier to one vertex and at most two homoclinic loops. The basin with its center is the increasing union of the bounded periodic disks and is a whole bounded complementary component of its frontier. A side-by-side figure eight cannot be its full frontier because each bounded component has only one lobe as frontier. Thus the alternatives are one simple loop and the nested pair. At a nested pair descend into its inner disk by the preceding lemma. This search has rank s(K), the number of saddles strictly inside its current search container, and strictly decreases on each descent. A simple frontier basin contains just its original center: no other zero can cross a nested regular periodic boundary. Its bounded side at the saddle occupies one quadrant. Indeed, a three-quadrant side contains the two unused separatrix half-branches strictly inside the basin, while every point of the basin other than its center belongs to a periodic orbit; this is impossible. The one interior descending saddle ray therefore enters the circle basin, and the other lies outside it and admits a short regular exit section. To use the cancellation statement, choose the sign of a continued scalar so that the center is a minimum; construction of that continued scalar remains an explicit upstream interface. Its one-sided rounded trace is supplied by the trace lemma; either a first essential loop already occurs in the regular annulus, or all those loops are null and an essential endpoint is a vanishing cycle. If the endpoint is null, choose exactly one leafwise nullhomotopy, smooth it relative to its C² boundary in finitely many intrinsic leaf charts, and use the fixed-cap cancellation supplier under its explicit scalar/block hypotheses. A regular null frontier has identity return holonomy and extends the same maximal annulus, so is not a stopping case. In a transverse outer collar there is no periodic orbit; a leafwise outer boundary is regular and essential. The outer iteration rank is the total number S of saddles of the current full disk. Each cancellation lowers S by one and leaves the prescribed boundary and all exterior singularities unchanged. Re-separate remaining singular leaves by the relative perturbation; this preserves S. The combined rank is lexicographic (S,s(K)) with an initial top search rank S. Every descent lowers its second entry, every cancellation lowers its first entry, and extending through a null regular orbit is absorbed into the one maximal-annulus step. No saddle graph can recur without either a strict source-disk descent or a genuine decrease of S. At S=0 the unique center has only regular frontier alternatives; the null extension and transverse-boundary exclusion force an essential endpoint, including the essential leafwise boundary alternative.

proposed_item_edits.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a $3$-manifold, and let $h:D^2\to M$ be a disk map in relative generic position. Suppose either (a) $h|_{\partial D^2}$ is a closed transversal, or (b) $h(\partial D^2)$ is a loop in one leaf and represents a nonzero class of that leaf. Then $F$ admits a vanishing cycle.
proposed_item_edits.strategy: Apply the relative singular-leaf separation and index count. Then apply the finite-rank selector/cancellation search. The outer boundary is unchanged, so its transverse or essential leafwise alternative remains available at every stage. The search either exhibits the required C² vanishing-cycle trace or decreases the full-disk saddle count. The terminal no-saddle case gives the trace. This is an integration-ready route conditional on the actual readiness of the period-frontier and cancellation suppliers; retain not-supplied until those prerequisites and the scalar/block interface stated below are closed.

proposed_item_edits.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F$ be a $C^2$ cooriented codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ and let $L$ be a leaf such that the inclusion-induced homomorphism $\pi_1(L)\to\pi_1(M)$ is not injective. Then $F$ admits a vanishing cycle.
proposed_item_edits.strategy: Choose a nonzero kernel class in π₁(L), represent it by a C² loop and span it by a C² ambient disk relative to that boundary. Put the disk in relative characteristic generic position and invoke the full disk-level lemma with its essential leafwise boundary alternative. This ambient disk is never treated as a leafwise cap. Keep not-supplied until the direct disk supplier is closed.

pinched_class_split.orientation: Write outer and inner based image loops as a and b with orientations chosen so the pinched basin boundary traversal is a b⁻¹.
cases: If a≠b, a rounded trace of the entire boundary traversal has nonzero class and can give a vanishing cycle only after its actual inward closed-orbit trace is proved.

If a=b≠1, both simple loops are essential but the whole traversal is null. Nullity of nearby pinched-basin circles does not establish nullity for displacements of either lobe separately. Descend into the inner source disk; do not cancel either loop on the basis of the product relation.
If a=b=1, fixed caps for the individual loops exist, but the proposed route still descends into the inner disk and obtains a simple-lobe cancellation. No pinched-annulus cancellation is needed.
If a≠b with exactly one trivial class, the product is essential; the same whole-traversal trace caveat applies. The uniform descent remains valid irrespective of image classes.

smallest_remaining_obstructions: The period-frontier item is currently not-supplied. This draft consumes its exact classification and does not recertify its flat-drift/Poincaré–Bendixson construction.

The cancellation item is currently not-supplied. The selected simple lobe supplies its topology/cap/exit picture, but its stated globally continued Euclidean-gradient scalar u₀ hypothesis must be constructed, or its claim separately repaired to an adapted descending field. It does not follow merely from the characteristic line field.

The cornered embedded source disk/cap seam requires finite relative C² smoothing and collar realization; this draft states the finite-chart construction but does not supply a schema item for that independent smoothing prerequisite.
forbidden_inferences: c−s=1 does not select a simple lobe.
Nullity of a b⁻¹ does not imply a=b=1.
An ambient source disk is not a leafwise null cap.
Finite singularities alone do not prove a compact separatrix frontier.
A count decrease inside K is not an inherited essential boundary class.
